Subject: Coordinated purge window & subprocessor rotation — MediControl

Hi Rachel and Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal at MediControl raised a hard requirement we need to lock in: any backup purge that affects EU customer data must be staged across regions to avoid a single-window cross-border effect and must align with our subprocessors rotation schedule for April/May. We also need to ensure logs tied to audit trails are retained for 90 days beyond the purge unless a formal exception is recorded.

Could you share a proposed staggered purge timeline and confirm which subprocessors will be active during each window? We have an upcoming regulatory inspection the week of May 6 and need the plan finalized by Apr 18 to include in our evidence binder.

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask.

We can do a geo-staggered purge that keeps EU data on EU-based subprocessors during the initial windows and shifts non-EU backups afterward. I attached a draft schedule (purge_schedule_v3.xlsx) with three candidate windows and a proposed subprocessor map per window (region -> subprocessor).

Key notes up front:
- We will not execute any purge that overlaps your inspection week (May 6). We can propose an early-May window that preserves logs for +90 days by default, or we can request a temporary log-retention exception where you restrict purging of audit logs only.
- Subprocessor rotation: two of Redwood's storage subprocessors will rotate maintenance windows the week of Apr 29 — we can pin variants to avoid mid-purge rotation, but that requires a brief service-configuration freeze (48 hours) and a signed DPA amendment acknowledging the freeze window.

Can Karthik and Kimberly confirm feasibility and legal language? If workable, Elena — is DocuSign or procurement email sufficient for your signatures?

Attachments: purge_schedule_v3.xlsx (staged purge windows, subprocessor map)

Thanks,
Rachel

Elena / Rachel — technical follow-up.

Thanks for the heads-up, Rachel. Quick points from infra:
- We can implement a three-stage purge: EU primary (week 1), APAC and US secondaries (week 2), final tombstone sweep (week 3). That prevents a single-shot cross-border purge. The schedule attached uses 12-hour rolling windows per region to minimize impact.
- Two subprocessors (StorageAlpha and NearStore EU) have pre-scheduled rotations Apr 29–May 2. To prevent a mid-purge subprocessor change we can either: (A) move MediControl's affected buckets to StorageAlpha-locked instances for the duration (requires a migration step ~6 hours), or (B) request a rotation freeze and include it in a DPA amendment. Option A has negligible legal overhead but needs ops time.
- Log retention exception: our default application logs are set to 30 days; audit logs are 365 days in the EU cluster. If you require 90 days post-purge specifically for forensic evidence, we can provide a temporary hold toggle and export a signed evidence bundle to your secure Drive link.

I've redlined the DPA to add a limited rotation-freeze clause and a temporary log-hold procedure — see attached dpa_amendment_redline.pdf.

Questions for MediControl: are you comfortable with (A) migration-to-locked-instance (ops-led) or (B) DPA amendment + rotation-freeze? Ops lead time for A is 48–72 hours scheduling.

Attachments: dpa_amendment_redline.pdf

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

karthik@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordinated purge window & subprocessor rotation — MediControl

Hi Elena — copying Marissa from commercial to align procurement/signature flow.

Legal summary of our position and next steps:
1) Rotation-freeze clause (drafted in the redline) is acceptable with the following limits: it is time-boxed to the agreed purge window + 7 days and applies only to the named subprocessors in the schedule.
2) Temporary log-hold: we will enable a forensic hold for audit logs for up to 120 days on request; Redwood requires a written justification and the specific log categories to avoid indefinite holds.
3) DPA amendment: please confirm the authorized signatory. We can do DocuSign; I have attached a signature page stub to speed execution.
4) Operational commitment: ops will require a 48- to 72-hour scheduling lead time for migration/locking steps. We cannot guarantee zero latency impact during the lock/migration window; we will provide a risk matrix in the final plan.

Requested from MediControl by EOD Apr 18:
- Choose migration (A) or rotation-freeze (B)
- Confirm signatory and preferred signing mechanism
- Confirm which log categories you require retained for 90/120 days

Attachments: signature_page_stub.pdf

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Thanks all — clear and helpful. Procurement confirms DocuSign is fine; I am the authorized signatory for this contract amendment. We reviewed the redline and prefer Option B (DPA amendment + rotation-freeze) to avoid any migration risk for our environment.

Log categories: please retain 'audit.access', 'data-deletion-events', and 'admin.change-history' for 120 days post-purge. We accept the rotation-freeze timebox (purge window + 7 days).

Action items we agree to:
- Redwood to send final DPA amendment via DocuSign today
- Redwood ops to schedule rotation-freeze and provide a risk matrix and final 12-hour rolling windows by Apr 18 17:00 UTC
- MediControl procurement to sign DocuSign within 48 hours of receipt

Attachments: backup_manifest.csv (requested manifest of affected buckets)
